statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress eases to 53 in the elevated band: the Saudi East-West pipeline is still shut with no restart timeline, WTI is marked $100.05 and a Wednesday policy decision is priced in the mid-eighties for an increase, while a further hour has passed with no verified escalation. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and the advance was broad, with seven of eight tracked megacaps higher and semiconductor gains spread across ARM, QCOM, INTC and AMD rather than concentrated in a single leader. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly ten hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. Third, the verified Gulf picture remains de-escalatory: Riyadh has paused retaliation at Baghdad's request, Iraq has removed its Maysan operations commander and closed the Iran-Iraq border crossing as a precaution, Tehran denies involvement, and Gulf foreign ministers are due to meet Iran in Salalah on Monday. No evidence-based danger window is published, because no window inside this horizon contains a tradeable session. Stress at 53 describes an unresolved Gulf supply picture and a hawkishly priced policy week; under the fixed mapping Stress does not alter the machine state on its own.
headline: Sixteen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, and the Gulf picture stayed de-escalatory this hour: the East-West pipeline remains shut with no restart timeline, while Iraq has dismissed its Maysan operations commander and closed the Iran-Iraq border crossing as a precaution ahead of Monday's Salalah talks.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95% with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%, a curve consistent with a hawkish policy path rather than a growth scare.

Friday's participation was broad rather than narrow. Seven of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher, and semiconductor strength was spread across ARM at +4.17%, QCOM at +2.88%, INTC at +2.61% and AMD at +2.49% while NVDA finished essentially flat. Breadth of that kind is a poor precursor to the squeeze-type one-way structure this Tail score is built to detect, and it is the main reason the conditional path into an eventual reopen is scored as gap exposure rather than as trend risk.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and already priced. Friday's inflation print showed headline consumer prices up 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, in line with consensus, with core slightly above forecast, and market-implied odds of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September meeting moved into the mid-eighties from the high sixties before the release. Equities rose anyway, which reporting attributed to the retreat in crude rather than to the inflation data itself. That meeting carries updated economic projections and a press conference thirty minutes after the decision, and the inherited calibration treats a multi-stage policy sequence as a case for care rather than an automatic block. Those are Wednesday checkpoints and sit outside this twenty-four-hour horizon.

The Gulf supply picture is the live unresolved item, and it did not deteriorate this hour. Saudi Arabia's 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline, which had been moving four to five million barrels a day or roughly four to five percent of global supply while bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, remains shut as a precaution while specialist teams secure it and assess its safety south of Medina; no restart timeline has been published, though a comparable pumping-station repair in April took three days. Hormuz itself has run far below normal throughput since March. Against that, Riyadh has paused retaliation at Baghdad's request while reserving its rights, Iraq has removed the Maysan operations commander and closed the Iran-Iraq border crossing as a precaution, Iran has denied involvement through official channels, and Gulf foreign ministers are due to meet Iran in Salalah on Monday to discuss shipping through the strait. Crude settled lower on Friday in response to those contacts, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81%, and WTI at $100.05, down 2.37%.

The binding constraint on this assessment is structural rather than informational. CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly ten hours after the last slot in this horizon. Every forecast hour therefore describes a market with no tape, in which shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension and holding near session extremes cannot be observed because they cannot occur. Conditional Tail rises from 6 to a ceiling of 11 across the horizon, and that drift is an accruing reopen-gap premium for unpriced weekend headlines, not a directional view. Shared supplementary cross-asset context was fresh this hour but flagged partial, with its calendar section unavailable; its healthy sections were latest-session and delayed by construction, and they only confirmed the independently verified Friday picture above, so they did not move any score.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 13:00 UTC on 11 September to 12:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens on the aftermath of the 12:30 UTC inflation print, which produced the only elevated reading of the period at Tail 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within an hour as NQ retraced, held between 13 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then fell to 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final fifteen slots sit at Tail 5 and 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 84 to 54 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly ten hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then drifts through 7, 8, 9 and 10 to a ceiling of 11 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs 53 to a 57 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage with no restart date, a Strait of Hormuz running far below normal since March, WTI marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline, and a 16 September policy decision with projections priced in the mid-eighties for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to 80, remaining inside the high band because the evidence set is complete and primary-sourced; the limitation is the freshness of price, not the coverage. The named checkpoints outside this horizon are the Sunday evening futures reopen, the Monday foreign ministers' meeting in Salalah and Wednesday's policy decision.
